# Slipway docs

> Build on Slipway. Ship Seaworthy. An editorial, RTL-ready, agent-native site template for GitHub Pages.

---

# Configure

Source: https://github.com/guide/configure/

Change the look of the site with a few lines in _config.yml.

## Tokens

Tokens restyle the whole site. Each one maps to a CSS variable.

```
slipway:
  tokens:
    radius: 0.75rem
```

## Languages

List each language with its URL prefix. The default language has an empty prefix.

```
slipway:
  languages:
    - { code: en, name: English, prefix: "" }
```

---

# Deploy

Source: https://github.com/guide/deploy/

Publish the built site on GitHub Pages.

## GitHub Pages

Push the repository and turn on Pages for the branch. Classic Pages builds the site with the same gem set the theme is tested against.

## Check before you publish

Run the checks, then read the report.

```
npm run check
```

---

# Overview

Source: https://github.com/guide/

What the guide covers and how the pages are organised.

## What this guide covers

The guide walks through a site from the first install to the first deploy.

## How the pages are organised

Each page is Markdown with a short front matter block. The sidebar comes from _data/navigation.yml, so adding a page to the sidebar is one line.

### Reading order

The previous and next links at the bottom follow the order of the sidebar.

---

# Install

Source: https://github.com/guide/install/

Add the theme to a site with the gem, a remote theme, or the template.

## Pick a mode

The theme works as a gem, through remote_theme, and after “Use this template”.

## Add the gem

```
# _config.yml
theme: slipway-theme
```

## Build

```
bundle exec jekyll build
```

Open _site/index.html to see the result.

---

# Write pages

Source: https://github.com/guide/write/

Front matter, headings, and code blocks in a documentation page.

## Front matter

Every page needs a title and a description.

```
---
title: My page
description: One sentence about the page.
layout: doc
---
```

## Headings

Use ## for sections and ### for subsections. The table of contents is built from them.

### Code blocks

A fenced block gets a copy button when scripts are available, and reads fine without them.

---

# Docs for a Slipway site

Source: https://github.com/

A documentation site built on the doc layout, with a sidebar, a table of contents, and previous and next links.

This site shows the doc layout on a small documentation set: install, configure, write, and deploy.
